column16: FULL TEXT READ (iMeta 2025). E1: compares its score with 12 published signatures (incl. TIDE), PD-L1 and TMB for patient ICB-response prediction, not gene-ranking methods. E2: pools 7 published CRISPR screens (17 datasets; melanoma, breast, colon, renal) into a mean-z gene ranking, then uses it only to pick CEP55 among score-associated genes; not ground truth for evaluating methods. E3: no purity adjustment (gene pairs and ComBat for batch; CIBERSORT/MCPcounter used descriptively). E4: 11 ICB cohorts, 6 cancer types, none pancreatic. Not prior art for the benchmark. Prior art for pooling CRISPR screens into one gene ranking

column16: FULL TEXT READ (Nat Mach Intell 2026). E1 partial: benchmarks gene-prioritization methods (OpenTargets, TargetDB, DepMap, CRISPR co-culture scores, non-graph ML) but not bulk-expression ranking methods. E2: positives are 260 clinical-stage immuno-oncology targets (CRI iAtlas), not CRISPR hits; CRISPR co-culture screens (Vredevoogd, Lawson) are input features and a competitor. E3 partial: scRNA-derived cell-type-specific interactomes used as features; bulk RNA regressed only on study/tissue source, no purity adjustment. E4: CPI1000+ with 9 tumor types, pooled/pan-cancer, pancreatic not analyzed. Design ideas worth borrowing: held-out genes, time-sliced validation, degree-preserving permutation nulls, explicit positive-unlabeled caveat
